correctness.rationale: For the exact double integrator with fixed u=-q-3v/2, h=1±delta iid equiprobable, 0<=delta<1, direct hold integration gives A(h) as in RESULT.md and A(1)^2=0. Independently formed the symmetric covariance lift K(delta^2) and checked every polynomial coefficient, det(I-K)=-(3z^3-11z^2+12z-2)/2 and det commutator=-delta^2(1-delta^2)^2. For delta>0 both step matrices invertible and their commutator has nonzero determinant; a positive-semidefinite Perron eigenmatrix of the adjoint cannot have rank one, hence is positive definite. The exact expected P-energy identity and norm equivalence establish the same all-initial-state trichotomy. The cubic has exactly one zero z*=0.202014738674272 in (0,1): r(0)=0, r(1)=5 and continuity, no other unit crossing. Thus delta*=0.449460497345731. The h=7/5 branch fails the Schur test (stable iff 0<h<4/3), while at delta=2/5 an exact rational P with entries 69675/10916,92725/21832,204927/43664 satisfies P-(A_-^T P A_- + A_+^T P A_+)/2=I with positive principal minors. Independently recomputed these identities symbolically. This is sampled-instant second-moment stability, not worst-case branch or almost-sure stability.

value.rationale: A sharp stochastic robustness margin for a canonical elementary sampled controller, with an explicit range where random switching stabilizes although one branch is unstable, is a meaningful quantitative control invariant. The result supplies a closed algebraic boundary and a concrete Lyapunov certificate; it is not merely a restatement of the generic second-moment test.
